rv.q: This musical took me by surprise: I expected something much less touching, gritty and moving.
The evening builds towards the resolution of that personal crisis – and achieves some hard-won hope for the future.
This musical – with its attractively earworm-infested score and lyrics by Sara Bareilles – is in no hurry to dispel this myth.
It’s also really wonderful, with the sweetness, crispness and comfort of the best homemade pie, and boasts one of the best scores to be written in recent years.
Adrienne Shelly would surely be delighted.
The show has cartoonish elements, but mostly subverts its moments of sentimentality and silliness, and there's a whole lot of humour baked into it.
Waitress has bags of charm and polish – but also a little too much sugar.
Similarly, ‘Waitress’ is made from the very finest ingredients, but often they don’t actually feel like ingredients that should have been put together.
If only everything about the show were as imaginative as its central notion.
I had a congenial enough time, but it's one of those productions where you can feel the plot grinding towards the next eruption of whoops from the stalls.
All in all, Waitress is a treat.
This sensational show feels like it’s in the West End for keeps.
The advantage for Waitress is Grammy ceremony semi-regular Sara Bareilles's eclectic and catchy score, and a clutch of winning performances...
What an delightfully warm, witty, wise and oh so wonderful treat.

Ultimately Waitress is a simple story, but this production is anything but plain. It has all the quality ingredients required to serve up a delicious, perfectly baked show, sprinkled with wholesome life lessons and a dash of unexpected spice.
If you’re a fan of Sara Bareilles, the film Waitress, or a beautifully written musical that will send you away with a song in your heart, and the taste of pie in your belly, this is for you.
Diane Paulus directs it all with a deft touch and perfect pace; pitching the comedy just right but slowing things down for the more heart-wrenching moments.
Perhaps this musical plays on the expected, but it doesn't make it any less delightful.
Yet it's one of a series of only fleeting highlights in a production, directed by Diane Paulus, that flatlines elsewhere.
Nonetheless, Waitress is not to all tastes.
Like those ghastly pies Jenna keeps preparing on stage - in scenes reminiscent of pantomime kitchen scenes - it all looks good until you taste it.
Boy is it an irresistible slice of musical theatre.

cn.t: Critics find this Broadway import a charming, bittersweet confection with Sara Bareilles' standout score and strong performances, particularly McPhee's vocals. Some find it overly sweet or lightweight, but most are won over by its warmth, wit, and surprising emotional depth.

vr.q: The show was absolutely amazing, it was as heartwarming and as lovely as it always is.
